minor.issue: DecisionIn (/app/backend/server.py:94) does NOT accept a `node_ids` field — only `linked_to`. Callers who want to seed a decision already linked to nodes must do a second call to POST /api/life-graph/decisions/{id}/nodes. This is fine but easy to overlook. The review-request wording 'creating a new decision with the same node_ids' implicitly assumes such a field. Test harness handles this by chaining the two calls; no product bug.

OPTIONAL: the /latest endpoint returns EITHER the raw snapshot dict (when present) OR {snapshot: null} — inconsistent envelope shape. Consider always wrapping: `{snapshot: <doc|null>}`. Currently the test tolerates both.

critical_code_review_comments: Context Assembler is a textbook read-only module: no writes to decisions, nodes, node_knowledge, life_edges, link_proposals, or memories — only inserts/updates on the dedicated `context_snapshots` collection. Verified by inspection of repository.py (all reads use projection {'_id': 0}, all writes touch self.col only) and service.py (calls repo.insert + repo.supersede_others only).

Idempotence is implemented cleanly: assemble() first computes the full snapshot (needed to derive context_hash), THEN checks repo.find_by_hash for an existing active snapshot with the same hash; if found and not force, returns the existing doc (same id). This is O(1) once the index (user_id,decision_id,context_hash) hits (server.py:1077 creates it).

Hashing excludes system signals (assembler.py:108: `hashable = [s for s in signals if s.source_module != 'system']`) — correct, otherwise now_iso/weekday/hour_of_day would flip the hash every call and break idempotence. Semantic changes (decision_signature, knowledge_versions, non-system signals) still propagate correctly.

Sensitive values are redacted BEFORE hashing (assembler.py:117: redact_for_hash(s.value, s.sensitivity)). This means the hash of a decision that references a plate does not depend on the plate's actual value — good privacy property AND stable across users who happen to share values.

Provider timeout + failure isolation is bulletproof: assembler.run_provider_safe wraps every coro in asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=8.0) and catches BaseException-adjacent (asyncio.TimeoutError, Exception) → returns a ProviderResult(error=...) with empty signals. The pipeline then filters out failed providers when merging raw signals but keeps their names in provenance.providers_failed + a warnings entry. Verified with monkeypatched graph_provider.

Data minimization via CATEGORY_ALLOWED_NODE_TYPES is enforced twice: (a) linked_nodes_provider filters kept nodes → drives which node_ids the knowledge/graph providers even query, so downstream signals are constrained by construction, and (b) graph_provider re-applies allowed_types on the traversal frontier. Belt+suspenders, but cheap and correct.

Feature flag adapter (attach_to_decision_context) is a real no-op when disabled and only populates ctx.signals['assembled_context'] — no side effects on DB, no re-ranking. Combined with the fact that NO existing rule in decision_engine reads that key, ranking is byte-stable in either mode. Verified empirically via top() before/after assemble.

server.py has grown to 1096 lines — past the 700-line 'must split' threshold. The context/* route group is small (5 endpoints, ~45 lines); consider extracting into `/app/backend/context_assembler/routes.py` mounted as its own APIRouter for cleaner separation.
